one_line: A shared map for negotiating group constraints and destinations.
what_it_does: Lets a group contribute shared, private, or agent-only needs, evaluates places live, and uses an agent to research missing venue information.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: agents can set up rooms, advocate for private constraints, research venues, and negotiate in shared live state; ordinary UI-driving agents would be substantially less reliable for privacy and structured negotiation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and transcript describe agent-assisted or fully delegated negotiation.
Private needs affect feasibility without revealing their reasons; agent-only needs remain local.
Transcript describes agent research filling hollow map pins for the whole group.
execution_rationale: The packaging, detailed workflow, transcript, and frame evidence form a coherent collaborative planning product, though some final workflow details are truncated and not directly observed.
execution_evidence: 174-second explainer transcript covers room setup, constraints, privacy, tradeoffs, research, and proposals.
Frame sheet visibly shows Spokes collaborative map/cards and participant markers.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: It addresses a common, concrete coordination problem while preserving sensitive constraints and reducing group-chat friction.
impact_evidence: Clear audience: groups choosing venues or plans together.
Transcript identifies dietary, budget, accessibility, privacy, and late-arriving constraints.
Shared result and private exit options directly address the stated failure mode.
creativity_rationale: Private constraint negotiation with agent advocacy inside a shared live map is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Private needs count without attribution or disclosure.
Agent-only needs and quantified opt-out tradeoffs are pursued as core mechanics.
Frame evidence shows a distinctive map-and-constraint interface.
usability_note: The described single composer, invite flow, and live map appear approachable; privacy and negotiation states may still be cognitively demanding.
red_flags: No direct runtime observation; agent invocation is described primarily by transcript.
Some transcript is truncated.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and unusually thoughtful collaborative interaction with credible demonstrated scope.

leverage_rationale: A structured agent surface connecting code, preview, and audit can materially improve reliable iterative implementation over generic UI driving, though the core editor remains usable without WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly exposes editor, preview, and WCAG audit to browser agents.
About text says the agent sees the same code, preview, and audit state.
Design-system and compatibility tools provide structured feedback for agent edits.
execution_rationale: The written scope is coherent but the submitted video is mislabeled as a Rick Astley music video and there is no transcript or frame evidence of the product, so execution is capped.
execution_evidence: About text specifies a detailed integrated editor workflow.
Facts report live demo.
Video title is unrelated and no usable product video evidence is available.
impact_rationale: Frontend developers and teams have a real recurring problem: accessibility and design-system quality are lost across disconnected tools; an integrated workflow addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Clear audience and pain point in inspiration text.
WCAG violations include impact, fix, and exact element.
Live preview, multi-device checks, and token drift checks support practical workflows.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-native editing and accessibility/design-system feedback is a fresh synthesis, though the editor category itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Same-tab code/preview/audit collaboration via WebMCP.

usability_note: Single-tab workflow is promising, but complexity of editor, audit, responsive preview, and compatibility panels may be high.
red_flags: Video title/content appears unrelated to the submission.
No visual product evidence in the submitted video.
standouts: Accessibility integrated into the agent editing loop
advance_reason: Strong concept and impact, but the broken/unrelated video leaves execution and actual WebMCP operation insufficiently evidenced.

creativity_evidence: Interactive periodic table and chemistry bench interaction.
Rejected combinations receive explanations and candidate searches stream/rank.

one_line: A consent-first task board that makes agent actions previewable and revocable.
what_it_does: Exposes task listing, proposal, and completion through scoped WebMCP tools with explicit sharing consent and human confirmation before writes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product's trust boundary: scoped tools, session consent, previews, and fail-closed behavior make agent collaboration safer and more legible than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Three named tools are exposed through document.modelContext.
Reads require explicit session-scoped consent; writes require separate approval.
Cancellation produces no write and unavailable WebMCP registers no tools.
execution_rationale: The public repository, live demo, and detailed consent semantics suggest a coherent focused implementation, but there is no video and no direct runtime observation.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo reported.
About text defines read/write flows, previews, confirmations, and fail-closed behavior.
Packaging frames are available but not a submitted video.
impact_rationale: Consent and action preview address a real trust problem for users delegating task-board work to agents, though the demonstrated domain is intentionally narrow.
impact_evidence: Explicit authority boundaries and revocable sharing.
Exact fields and status transitions are previewed before writes.
Audit-oriented task-board use case is concrete.
creativity_rationale: Human approval and privacy semantics are thoughtfully embedded in the WebMCP interaction model, even though task boards are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Existence-disclosure protection for completion reads.
Session-scoped sharing plus separate write approvals.
Fails closed when WebMCP is unavailable.
usability_note: The consent and preview flow is clear in principle but adds friction to simple task actions.
red_flags: No video evidence of an end-to-end agent invocation.
Narrow task-board scope.
advance_reason: Clear, credible WebMCP-native trust model with sufficient implementation evidence for advancement.

one_line: An agent-and-human workspace for proposing, approving, and proving accessibility fixes.
what_it_does: Scans a synthetic checkout, stages bounded remediations, requires human approval or revision, applies approved patches, and replays an 11-step keyboard journey.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates shared structured state across agent actions and human decisions, with bounded tools, approval gates, patch identifiers, and deterministic verification that generic UI automation would reproduce less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes phase-scoped tools for replay, scan, stage, and apply.
Agent and human actions share browser-local state and immutable activity records.
Apply accepts only approved proposal identifiers; human revision can replace a proposal.
execution_rationale: The video transcript gives unusually complete end-to-end evidence from six baseline failures through approvals, application, replay, and all assertions passing.
execution_evidence: 144-second video transcript covers baseline, six findings, six proposals, five approvals, one rejection/revision, apply, and replay.
Final state reports zero open issues and 11 assertions passing.
Version comparison and 19 immutable activity records are described.
impact_rationale: Accessibility remediation is a real high-value problem for developers and users; the workflow closes the gap between finding issues and proving fixes without removing human judgment.
impact_evidence: Concrete barriers include labels, focus order, keyboard trap, announcements, contrast, and accessible naming.
The replay verifies keyboard focus, labels, status announcements, errors, and final action.
Human approval and wording review preserve accountable decisions.
creativity_rationale: The full scan-to-review-to-fix-to-replay lifecycle, with proposal revision and durable evidence, is a memorable and deeply pursued agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Bounded staged changes rather than silent mutation.
Human rejection and revised wording are linked in the audit trail.
Before/after deterministic proof is part of the product, not an afterthought.
usability_note: The staged approval flow supports trust and review, though six findings and audit detail may be dense for casual users.
red_flags: Demo uses a synthetic checkout fixture, so generalization beyond the fixture is unproven.
standouts: Human revision is a first-class decision
advance_reason: Best-evidenced packet: strong WebMCP leverage, complete workflow proof, and meaningful accessibility impact.

one_line: Browser-native audio context exposed to agents in real time.
what_it_does: Exposes live page and meeting audio through WebMCP, supporting local microphone and WebRTC audio, captions, provider-independent processing, and an extension for sites the team does not control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes transient live audio that DOM/UI automation cannot naturally provide, allowing the agent and human to attend to the same meeting or media stream in real time.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly contrasts audio access with DOM, network, screenshots, and input automation.
Page and meeting audio are exposed incrementally while events happen.
Site package and browser extension cover controlled and uncontrolled sites.
execution_rationale: The live demo, public repo, detailed transcript, and stated lightweight server architecture support a coherent ambitious prototype, though some audio/provider behavior is not visually verified here.
execution_evidence: 158-second demo transcript describes live audio, WebRTC meeting, captions, and agent use.
Public repo and live demo reported.
Server provisions tokens/signaling without receiving media or transcript text.
impact_rationale: Agents that can hear tutorials, webinars, and meetings can reduce repeated transcription/copying and support real-time shared understanding for users with legitimate audio-context needs.
impact_evidence: Clear problem: agents otherwise miss browser audio.
Use cases include meetings, tutorials, and webinars.
Privacy-conscious architecture keeps media/transcripts out of the server.
creativity_rationale: Treating live browser audio as a first-class WebMCP modality is a genuinely novel and technically ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Bridges browser-owned media streams into agent context incrementally.
Supports both native site integration and extension fallback.

usability_note: Real-time provider setup, permissions, captions, and audio context may be complex; transcript mentions provider access but packet leaves exact onboarding unclear.
red_flags: Transcript is noisy and does not clearly identify every agent invocation.

advance_reason: Highly differentiated WebMCP capability with a credible live demo and strong potential value.
